contexts.text: For the sake of acquiring dignity or opulence.

The natural man is in his bliss when he is opulent above others, and possesses the wealth of the world; but the spiritual man... when in the Knowledges of truth and good, which are his opulence... Nor does he spurn opulence, because by its means he can be in exercise, and in the world. See AC 5159:3.
(The idea) that spiritual good is not possible in worldly opulence. (See Riches.)

He who believes from the heart that of himself he possesses nothing, knows nothing, is not wise, and has no power, in Heaven is rich and abounds; for the Lord gives him all wealth; for he is wiser than all others, and richer than all others; he dwells in most magnificent palaces, and in the treasures of all the riches of Heaven.
All their wealth () = all the scientifics which they have acquired for themselves. Wealth = scientifics; for spiritual wealth is nothing else.
The profane things which they conceal beneath their external sanctity, are that they intend nothing else than to become the greatest and most opulent of all...

In the spiritual life there are no other riches than the Knowledges of good and truth; and no other possessions and inheritances than the felicities of life which are from goods and the derivative truths.
Who are in Heaven, and yet had been opulent, and some of them among the most opulent.

The Divine Providence has as its end the eternal salvation of man; thus not... his eminence and opulence... (for) eminence for the most part begets the love of self, and opulence the love of the world... and therefore such things are given to the evil; and also to the good if they are not out of place for them and do not lead them away from Heaven.

Besides, in eminence and opulence there is worldly, but not eternal happiness; hence they are for the wicked as well as the good; and if not [given] to the good, it is to prevent them from being turned away from good.
They place nothing real in faith and charity... but solely in opulence and eminence...

(Thus) those who are in eminence and opulence above others, can look above themselves to the Lord equally with those who are not in eminence and opulence; for they look above themselves when they have eminence and opulence as means, and not as the end.
It then never came into anyone's mind to attack the inheritance of another, and thence to acquire for themselves opulence and dominion.
Those who are in evil from the love of the world... estimate the neighbour solely from his opulence; thus his wealth; and not himself.
Those who trust in the Divine... if they become opulent, do not set the heart on opulence.
He who has opulence as the end...
(The idea that) man comes to opulence not from any Divine aid...
That eminence and opulence in the world are not real Divine blessings... They seduce many, and turn them away from Heaven. NJHD 270.
The rich in Heaven are in opulence above the rest. Described.
Such as had been their uses in the world, such is their opulence.
That opulence and eminence... are not regarded by the Lord as blessings; but only as means for man's life in the world. References.
The Lord leads man to regard (opulence) not for the sake of himself, but for the sake of use; thus that it belongs to uses, and thence to himself; and not to himself, and thence to uses.

Most of those who in the natural world had become great and opulent, and in their honours and riches had looked to themselves only, at first speak about God... But as they then manifestly see the Divine Providence, and, from it, their final lot... they conjoin themselves with devils...
When he sees the evil in glory and opulence...
Besides, what is... opulence greater or less? Is it in itself anything but an imaginary affair?
(Inequality as to opulence, a cause of cold between consorts.)
Opulences in Heaven are the endowments of being wise; according to these wealth is given them in sufficiency.
These two (evil) loves may reign more... with the poor than with the opulent...
The Angels are... most opulent. Described.
Fat and opulent () = fun of the good of love and the derivative truths; for... opulent is said of truths.
The tenth law of the Divine Providence is, That man, from his Own prudence, has led himself to eminence and to opulence, although these seduce... General article.

There are two things which principally affect the lower minds of men: eminence and opulence... opulence is of the love of money and possessions, (Continued. See Eminence. AE 1187:3. AE 1190:2. AE 1191:2. AE 1191:end.)
That... those who have as the end opulence and gain in the world... do not see and find anything of genuine truth in the Word. General article.
4. In the Heavens, each one has magnificence, opulence, and happiness, according to his fidelity, sincerity, and justice there.
